units.sentence: First version of this page.
units.reason: Page history.

framing_issues.text: Residents' names, roads and home addresses are left out of this page and its passages.
framing_issues.issue: Privacy. workspace.md, home.md and the display strings name no private person and no road. But two passages the page cites (P-011 and P-012, cited at lines 40, 41, 80, 144, 203 and 207) carry the full name of the staff's witness, while P-014 was trimmed to drop another witness's name. If this witness is a private person rather than an official, the name should be cut from those passages the same way. I could not tell from the passages which he is.

framing_issues.text: Evidence: Supported.
framing_issues.issue: The only 'Supported' summary on the page goes to the staff card, though its header also says 'Uncertain' and the card lists VoltaGrid's conflicting account. Cards 1, 4 and 5 restate their weaker label. This reads as a grade in favor of one side.

framing_issues.text: No filing we read says whether such an order would change the pollution neighbors describe.
framing_issues.issue: Uneven caveat. Outcome B's benefit to the filers is qualified, while Outcome A's 'Who pays' (line 109) presents the pollution as following from the outcome with no such caveat.

framing_issues.text: says a supplier's other consumers could absorb the cost of lines built for customers who are "picked off."
framing_issues.issue: Shown alone to EMC customers. It does not say the statement is about suppliers in general, and that the site is in Georgia Power's territory (P-061), not an EMC's. Line 109 carries that caveat; this line does not.

framing_issues.text: The PSC's staff
framing_issues.issue: Missing context. The witness testifies for the 'Public Interest Advocacy Staff' (P-073). The page says 'the PSC's staff' throughout, which a new reader may take to be the decision-makers' own neutral advisers.
Consistency. The docket page (P-001) shows 'Date: 07/02/2026'; the page gives Jul 13 for the petition (P-002) and Jul 2 for the notice of violation (P-028) and does not explain the docket date.

framing_issues.text: power companies
framing_issues.issue: Georgia EMC is a trade association, not a power company; the line also states effects as fact where the sources are each party's claim.

framing_issues.text: No final vote is set.
framing_issues.issue: Unscoped and undated, unlike line 36. Two orders could not be read (lines 37, 44).

framing_issues.text: how soon the data center could get power another way
framing_issues.issue: Missing context. Georgia Power calls VoltaGrid's service 'bridge power' to a customer 'slated to become a Georgia Power customer' (P-061) and the petition speaks of 'short-term power plants' (P-032). The page never says the service is described as temporary, while it does say the plant would 'run all year'.

framing_issues.text: The number of filers does not decide the legal question
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference. 'filers' means the petitioners at line 8 and the responding parties here.

framing_issues.text: "does not dispute that these issues are essential to this case,"
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference. 'these issues' (line 39) and 'the question' (line 159) are not placed for the reader; in P-025 the question is whether VoltaGrid is an 'electric supplier'.

framing_issues.text: first filed Nov 9, 2026
framing_issues.issue: Vague. 'first filed' implies a later filing the page never mentions.

framing_issues.text: "considers potential risks to other Georgia Power customers."
framing_issues.issue: The source sentence begins 'Briefly,' (P-074). Dropping it makes the treatment sound fuller than the witness says it is.

framing_issues.text: No other filing we read backs the stranded-cost point with figures
framing_issues.issue: Ambiguous. Reads as if Georgia EMC's own filing gives figures; line 183 says no filing does.

framing_issues.text: "is the antithesis of a monopoly, and is negotiating bespoke rates with a sophisticated counterparty."
framing_issues.issue: Terms left unexplained for a grade 6-8 reader, here and elsewhere: 'antithesis', 'bespoke rates', 'counterparty' (99), 'stranded' (100, 174), 'Conversion Assets' (145), 'condemnation power' (156), 'conflates' (157), 'statement of work' (144), 'electric supplier' (87), 'retail' (148), 'record' (39), 'standing' (205), 'rebuttal testimony' (80).

framing_issues.text: a 2001 Georgia law on plants that power their owners
framing_issues.issue: The gloss comes from one provision as the petition quotes it (P-036); 'cogeneration' itself is never explained. Likewise 'electric membership corporation' (lines 16, 74) is not in any passage; P-062 says 'electric distribution cooperatives'.

framing_issues.text: testified on Oct 9, 2026
framing_issues.issue: Consistency. Line 155 says 'testimony dated Oct 9, 2026' for the same document; 'testified on' suggests live testimony.

framing_issues.text: supplies natural gas to the plant
framing_issues.issue: Lines 20-22 use the present tense ('supplies', 'turns', 'pays'); the sworn statement is in the future tense and P-068 says the plant had not started on Oct 9.

framing_issues.text: Decided after the Dec 9 hearing:
framing_issues.issue: Consistency. Line 39 says the request to dismiss is still pending and could end the case before the hearing.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power says the site is in its assigned territory and Serverfarm is slated to become its customer.
framing_issues.issue: Uneven. Outcome A names who benefits directly; here Georgia Power's statement is listed under 'Who benefits' without saying whether or how it benefits.

framing_issues.text: Where the money comes from
framing_issues.issue: Heading suggests public money; the items describe a private contract, and only item 5 says so indirectly.
